articles.title_orig: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
articles.title_zh: Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
articles.content_orig:
The tech industry needs this to go well. So does Wall Street.
Anthropic's IPO filing on Monday puts the Claude creator in position to pursue what could be the largest initial stock offering in history. Investors are already measuring the 5-year-old company's potential market cap in the trillions, putting it in a category with the world's most valuable companies.
It's a critical moment for the whole tech sector, as the artificial intelligence boom has been largely driven by two companies: Anthropic and OpenAI. The latter has confidentially filed to go public, but has said a debut likely won't take place until 2027.
Meanwhile, the stock market is showing signs of jitters on the AI trade. Neoclouds and data center companies have been getting pummeled, prompting Australia's Firmus to withdraw its IPO plans and for SK Hynix's U.S.-based Solidigm unit to do the same.
Now, all eyes turn to Anthropic , which is betting that investors will look past over $80 billion in losses in the first half of the year, and see the 14-fold increase in revenue as a reflection of seemingly insatiable demand for the company's leading models and services.
"If it underperforms expectations, it'll be a little bit of a house of cards," said Jai Das, co-founder of Sapphire Ventures whose career in tech investing dates to the 1990s.
Anthropic's business is deeply entwined with tech megacaps. Close to half its revenue comes from Claude being sold through cloud divisions at Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet , which all hold investments in the company. In the IPO, some $77 billion in notes can be issued to Amazon , Broadcom and Google , while Microsoft and Nvidia agreed to invest $15 billion as the company builds up its computing capacity. Chips from Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices , Amazon and Google are powering Anthropic's development.
Cloud providers are ratcheting up capital expenditures to meet demand, and memory manufacturers are fighting shortages to prioritize AI chips. And there's the debt factor. Alphabet, with its investment-grade credit rating, committed to backstopping Anthropic for a data center in Texas. Broadcom , which helps Google develop chips for AI labs, is creating financing pools to help Anthropic and OpenAI deploy high-performance models, CEO Hock Tan told analysts earlier this year.
For public market investors, more than one-third of the value of the S&P 500 comes from tech's trillion-dollar companies, which are all, to varying degrees, going deep in AI. Beyond that, there are software giants like Adobe and Salesforce that have integrated with Anthropic's Claude assistant.
And in the private markets, check sizes have ballooned but IPOs are few and far between. Bessemer Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures both told CNBC that Anthropic is their biggest investment ever.
"If they don't perform well, they will become the bellwether for AI," said Brad Bernstein, a managing partner at growth equity firm FTV Capital. "Their valuation will reflect that performance variation, and then it'll just be a trickle-down effect to all the stuff going on with the excess capital that's getting poured into the venture AI world. Everything is going to have to sort of be reset."
Anthropic will be the third company to go public with a valuation above $1 trillion, after Saudi Aramco and Elon Musk's SpaceX , which debuted in June. OpenAI could be the fourth.
Revenue at Anthropic has been multiplying at a staggering pace as businesses adopt the company's coding and productivity tools. Second-quarter revenue soared to $11.56 billion from $787 million a year earlier.
The company held almost $132 billion in cash, equivalents and short-term investments at the end of June. And after five quarters of operating losses, Anthropic reported $974 million in operating income for the second quarter.
"It is, I think, better than feared," said Rohit Kulkarni, partner and chief AI officer at Burnham Park Capital Markets, referring to the financials. "There could have been more negative tidbits."
One source of concern in some corners of the investing universe is the emergence of so-called open-weight models, which are cheaper for businesses to access and allow for customization and flexibility in terms of where users access the models.
In the prospectus, the only two competitors Anthropic named were OpenAI and Google, though the company said it faces competition from a "broader set of model providers," including open-weight or open-source models.
Anthropic says it's all very early, with Fortune 500 companies committing less than 0.1% of their total expenses to its models and services in the latest quarter. Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager at Founder ETFs, says that's part of the investment thesis.
"I think there's going to be room for frontier models like Anthropic and OpenAI and SpaceX, and I think there will be room for open-weight models," Monaghan said. "It's way too soon to say that one is going to disintermediate the other."
With hyperscaler spending on AI infrastructure set to reach into the trillions of dollars, Sapphire's Das said there's understandable concern about a market glut. But he compares it to the telecommunications and dot-com bubble of the late 1990s, when companies flooded the market with fiber-optic equipment. Eventually, the infrastructure got used, although plenty of companies went belly up in the interim.
"Long term, I don't think there is a lack of demand," Das said.
A lackluster debut could push out OpenAI's offering even further and cause investors to rethink its lofty valuation. At the same time, rising interest rates mean it's getting costlier for companies to raise debt.
David Trainer, CEO of financial research firm New Constructs, wrote in a report last month that the AI boom has been built on the view that cheap credit and access to the capital markets will be "readily available."
"If AI liquidity dries up, and there are clear signs it is, we see large, 20%, downside risk in the S&P 500, with most of that concentrated in the valuation of AI-related stocks," Trainer wrote.
Industry experts take a different approach, focusing on the power and rapid proliferation of the technology. Claude Opus 5.5 Max performs better than any other model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, an industry benchmark .
Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy said the technology is only becoming more essential.
"Anthropic and OpenAI have by now demonstrated their ability to stay at the frontier of AI and keep pushing innovation," Ramaswamy said. "They're incredible companies that are doing a big service to humanity by expanding the frontier of what is possible, and we are very much rooting for them to be public and very successful companies."
Still, Snowflake is experimenting with low-cost open-weight models from China's Moonshot AI, DeepSeek and Zhipu.
"We spend a lot on internal AI because we want to get as much efficiency as we can," Ramaswamy said.

articles.title_orig: Iran talks Middle East security, urges region to get US influence out
articles.title_zh: Iran talks Middle East security, urges region to get US influence out
articles.content_orig:
Footage from a polling station in Rio de Janeiro showed electoral officials retrieving the voting results reports and disconnecting the machines after the first round of voting on Oct. 4, 2026. (Reuters)
SAO PAULO, Brazil— About 125 million Brazilians voted Oct. 4 on machines that print no paper ballots. Less than four hours after polls closed, the country knew its presidential election was headed to a runoff between conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro and leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva .
That process has been in place for over three decades, and Brazilians have become accustomed to its speed, simplicity, accuracy and routine. The system is robustly audited, completely disconnected from the Internet, and is the largest digital voting system deployed on the planet.
Eleven days before the U.S. midterms, Brazil’s system, analysts say, could offer Americans a more secure way to vote.
The system has been widely praised and was also mentioned in President Donald Trump’s 2025 executive order on elections , where he cited Brazil’s biometric voter identification as an example. Yet Brazil’s count runs partially on the kind of paperless machines that the president has vowed to scrap.
STATE DEPARTMENT CONSIDERS SHARING PASSPORT RECORDS FOR VOTER CITIZENSHIP CHECKS
Election workers prepare and seal electronic voting machines ahead of the upcoming general elections in Brasilia, Brazil, on Sept. 23, 2026. (Mateus Bonomi/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Over the years, Brazil merged federal, state and municipal databases into a digital voting record, whereby voter identity, eligibility and single ability to vote can (and usually must) be verified biometrically. Nearly 9 in 10 voters unlock the machines with a fingerprint.
Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court, or TSE, which designs the machines and oversees elections, says there has been no proven fraud since their 1996 debut. The 499,248 machines used on Oct. 4 never connected to the internet. Their software was open to inspection by parties, universities and watchdogs for 11 months before being digitally signed and sealed in public. Last December, the Brazilian government invited a record 149 outsiders to try to break the system; evaluators concluded nothing they found could alter results or reveal how anyone voted.
An electronic voting machine at a Regional Electoral Court (TRE) facility in Brasilia, Brazil, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. (Ton Molina/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
On election day, randomly drawn machines are fed paper ballots on camera as federal auditors and foreign observers watch and specifically track results.
Meanwhile, at closing, every machine used at every polling station prints its tally, which is then posted in front of the polling place with a QR code, so anyone can check it against the national count. In an email to Fox News Digital, TSE said each file’s digital signature "confirms that the result was produced by the electronic voting machine registered for that polling station."
Karina Stange Calandrin, a political scientist and professor at Instituto Brasileiro de Mercado de Capitais (IBMEC), says the system combines three traits rarely found together: voting is electronic, votes hashed to voter eligibility are stored locally in the machine and tallying is automated.
"It is an extremely secure and safe system. The machines never connect to the Internet and even the central database system used to transmit tallied votes to TSE must match results issued physically and locally by each individual machine without human interference," she said. Corrupting it, she added, would require breaking the seal of each machine and installing software that wouldn’t match the TSE’s version, automatically disqualifying its tally — a scale of collusion so large that it "simply could not pass undetected."
COLOMBIA'S 'EL TIGRE' SECURES PRESIDENCY AS LEFTIST RIVAL FINALLY CONCEDES DEFEAT
Brazil's right-wing senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party (PL) gestures next to federal deputy and candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, Douglas Ruas (L) during a campaign rally on the eve of the general election, in Campo Grande neighborhood, in the western zone of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil on October 3, 2026. Brazilians go to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026. (Douglas SHINEIDR / AFP via Getty Images)
The machines passed their toughest political test in 2022, when former President Jair Bolsonaro , now serving a 27-year sentence for plotting to overturn his 2022 defeat, spent years attacking their credibility without evidence. Bolsonaro is presently serving time under house arrest.
This year, for the first time, a Bolsonaro appointee ran the TSE: Justice Kassio Nunes Marques. Bolsonaro’s eldest son, Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, finished first with 47% to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s 45%. The machines at the center of the senior Bolsonaro’s controversy may yet hand victory to his son.
Florencia Ferrer, CEO of e-stategiapublica, which has audited elections in 17 countries, has no doubt the Brazilian system is the most modern and secure in the world. "In India votes are electronic, but each voter gets a printed version of their vote to take home, which weakens voter safety and augments coercion rates," she says, adding that Estonia’s internet voting and the Philippines’ electronically tallied paper ballots carry their own risks.
An engineer from the University of São Paulo’s Polytechnic School who audited the machines in 2014, and declined to be named due to the sensitive nature of his work, agreed. "While no system is completely infallible... we have found no traces of tampering, wrong-doing or malicious intent," he told Fox News Digital.
Still, some defend higher scrutiny. Security researchers say a clean record is not proof enough, and the Carter Center said voters should at least see a printed version of their ballot deposited into a separate area of the machine; otherwise, results integrity rests on software alone. Germany’s top court ruled in 2009 that voters must be able to check their ballot without expert help, effectively barring a Brazilian-like system.
Brazil’s machine has traveled mostly on loan to countries in Latin America , Africa and Asia. Paraguay adopted it permanently in 2006, with machines that now print each individual vote.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Brazil's President and presidential candidate Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (C) waves next to Vice-President Geraldo Alckmin (L) and to his candidate for São Paulo's governor, Fernando Haddad during a campaign rally on the eve of the general election, in São Paulo, Brazil on October 3, 2026. Brazilians go to the polls on Oct. 4, 2026, (Luis Robayo/AFP Via Getty Images)
"It’s obvious Washington and the remainder of the U.S. are way behind both technology as well as security when it comes to polling on voting day," Ferrer said. U.S. elections are run in thousands of local jurisdictions under 50 sets of state rules and about 30% of 2024 ballots came by mail , which is slower to process. Brazil has one national election authority, compulsory voting and no mail-in ballots.
Brazilians will vote this coming Sunday on Oct. 25. The winner is expected to be known and certified in under five hours.
"The question is not whether Brazil has invented a perfect voting machine. No voting system is perfect. It is whether democracies can combine the speed and consistency of digital tabulation with independent verification, public scrutiny and rules that citizens across the political spectrum have reason to trust," Ferrer said.
Solly Boussidan is an international journalist covering Latin America for Fox News Digital. He has previously covered international affairs, war, finance and travel for several U.S. and international outlets. He is currently based in Brazil.

articles.title_orig: Dollar General sued by FTC and 20 states, accused of overcharging customers
articles.title_zh: Dollar General sued by FTC and 20 states, accused of overcharging customers
articles.content_orig:
The Federal Trade Commission and 20 states on Monday sued Dollar General, accusing the budget retailer of charging customers more for products than it advertised.
The chain, which operates 21,000 stores nationwide, allegedly mislabeled prices for years, "extracting millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges," the FTC alleged.
"Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last," Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection, said in a statement .
The FTC added that American consumers depend on Dollar General's advertised low prices to make ends meet on tight budgets, while prices that don't reflect advertised deals make it impossible for them to manage household finances.
The agency filed its complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee, Dollar General's home state.
"Our goal is 100% accuracy between shelf and register prices in every store," Dollar General said in a statement. "As with other retailers and despite our policies and procedures, occasional price discrepancies can occur. When that happens, our store teams are instructed, empowered, and expected to make things right for the customer. In recent years, we have enhanced our price-accuracy processes and remain committed to continuous improvement."
Dollar General said it was made aware of the FTC's investigation in early February.
According to the suit, thousands of Dollar General stores unlawfully overcharged shoppers.
Dollar General "has for years engaged in deceptive conduct that harms the very consumers it claims to serve," the FTC and states allege in the suit. "Although Dollar General promises convenience, low prices, and value, the company has routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags, and advertisements. This pattern of inaccurate pricing has persisted for years and affects millions of purchases across the country."
The company also faced thousands of consumer complaints claiming it failed to honor advertised prices at checkout, a sign Dollar General knowingly harmed customers, according to the FTC.
The suit seeks a permanent injunction, along with monetary and other relief.
In its statement, Dollar General said, "FTC staff also demanded a monetary amount that was untethered to — and orders of magnitude larger than — any realistic assessment of amounts attributable to pricing discrepancies."
The company said it "worked tirelessly and in good faith to resolve this matter without litigation," including an "alternative, and in our view, more reasonable, manner of calculating potential settlement ranges."
"Although we respect the FTC's role in protecting American consumers and the State representatives' role in protecting the citizens of their respective states, we will defend this litigation vigorously," it said.
The FTC leveled the unfair pricing allegations against Dollar General as other retailers face scrutiny over how they charge shoppers. Consumer advocates say retailers are developing new artificial intelligence-enabled technology that could be used to charge consumers different prices .
Groundwork Collaborative, a nonprofit think tank focused on economic policy, led an investigation into grocery-shopping platform Instacart and found that in a trial, it had used AI to simultaneously show customers different prices for the same goods from the same store.

articles.title_orig: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
articles.title_zh: UPS CEO says delivery company will make more money on slightly fewer holiday deliveries
articles.content_orig:
United Parcel Service on Tuesday reported third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year guidance.
The guidance raise comes after the company already upped its outlook last quarter . UPS now said it's projecting full-year consolidated revenue of approximately $92.6 billion, up from its previous expectations of $91.2 billion, as well as fourth-quarter revenue of $25.7 billion.
Shares of UPS rose slightly in morning trading.
Here's how the company performed in its third quarter, compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
For the quarter ended Sept. 30, UPS reported net income of $1.16 billion, or $1.37 per share, down slightly from net income of $1.31 billion, or $1.55, the year prior. Adjusting for one-time expenses, UPS reported earnings per share of $1.69. Revenue rose 6.7% to $22.9 billion.
In its domestic segment, the company said it saw a 4.5% increase in revenue, while its international segment had a 7.1% rise in revenue. Its supply chain solutions business saw an 18.2% revenue increase, which UPS said was primarily driven to growth in forwarding and logistics, including healthcare . On a call with analysts, CEO Carol Tomé said healthcare revenue exceeded $3 billion for the third consecutive quarter.
The company had previously said it expected its third-quarter domestic revenue to be flat and for domestic average daily volume to fall due to seasonal declines and the glide down with Amazon .
"We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network," Tomé said on the call. "All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."
UPS has been in the midst of a turnaround under Tomé's leadership, working to create a leaner business model and leveraging automation to position the company for growth.
As the company prepares for its peak holiday season, Tomé said the consumer remains resilient, and the growth in average daily volume between the third and fourth quarters will be consistent with last year. However, fourth-quarter domestic average daily volume is expected to fall due to the reduction with Amazon.
She added that nearly 70% of all packages will flow through an automated process this holiday season.

articles.title_orig: Why Anthropic's IPO contrasts the 'cult of Elon Musk' at SpaceX and Tesla
articles.title_zh: Why Anthropic's IPO contrasts the 'cult of Elon Musk' at SpaceX and Tesla
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
In the first mega IPO of 2026, SpaceX ( SPCX ) singled out one person in its prospectus as the shot caller: none other than the world's richest person, Elon Musk.
The next big IPO of the year — Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ), which could be the largest of all time — is run more by a committee of founders. That's a good thing given its mission and structures, according to veteran dealmaker Jim Neeson.
"I would say having seven founders working together can make it where it's not just like a cult of Elon Musk, right?" the Connor Group founding executive said on Sozzi Unleashed . "You actually have it where you have a consortium of people making decisions, which I actually think can be a good thing."
Neeson noted that Anthropic is a public benefit company with seven founders who collectively own 50.1%.
"You have a board that will be approved by sort of a trust fund. And then you also have a business where it's not just going to be about profits. It's also going to be sort of the social benefit piece that's built into their doctrine," he explained.
Anthropic's founders are CEO Dario Amodei and his sister and president, Daniela Amodei, as well as Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, and Chris Olah. The consortium left OpenAI ( OPAI.PVT ) to start Anthropic in January 2021.
The seven co-founders will be issued new Class F common stock as part of the IPO, giving them majority control of the company — something Neeson said investors will have to navigate.
"If you look at Meta, [and] you also look at Google, you had very strong founders," Neeson said. "A lot of times that is the venture capital case. I want founders that can make strong decisions and not be beholden to sort of quarterly type of trends."
"This is going to be a different type of structure out there, and it's going to be tested," he added. "We've never seen it, especially at this scale, especially at these growth rates. So I would say that's one thing analysts and investors are going to be looking very closely at."
The group looks to be managing the financials relatively well.
Anthropic's first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, the prospectus showed. The filing also discloses an $80.7 billion first-half net loss, a strong signal of aggressive AI spending in the years ahead.
On an adjusted basis, Anthropic posted $1.62 billion in operating income through the first six months of 2026 compared to a loss of $1.85 billion last year.
Investment bankers are reportedly aiming for an astronomical listing valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion.
Anthropic could debut on public markets before the end of November. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

articles.title_orig: Oil Futures Fall as Market Holds Out Hope for Middle East Diplomacy
articles.title_zh: Oil Futures Fall as Market Holds Out Hope for Middle East Diplomacy
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
HOUSTON, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Oil futures settled down by almost $2 a barrel on Tuesday, though prices remain near six-month highs due to the disruption of shipping around the Middle East, and an agreement to end the US-Israeli ‌war with Iran remains elusive.
Brent crude futures settled down $1.93, or 1.67%, at $113.88 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude settled down $1.86, ‌or 1.83%, at $99.90.
Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei met Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei on Tuesday, a day after holding talks with representatives of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan.
State ​media said Khamenei had emphasized the importance of pursuing Iran's interests and maintaining its conditions for ending the war.
The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media said.
The outlook for peace remains uncertain as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis renewed attacks on key oil producer Saudi Arabia. The Houthis said on Tuesday that they had struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, the biggest in ‌the kingdom, with a ballistic missile.
"Continued Houthi attacks ⁠on Saudi Arabia and the expanding military presence in the Gulf are keeping supply risks in place, even as diplomatic headlines encourage some of the recent premium to unwind," said Gelber & Associates analysts in a note.
October has ⁠been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, according to data compiled by the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, a think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.
Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has risen but the number ​of ​vessel attacks has increased, with risks likely to become more acute if US ​naval support wavers, UBS said.
Brent prices surged to more ‌than $117 a barrel last week, their highest since April, after a wave of Iranian attacks on tankers around the strait.
UBS said it expects Brent prices to stay elevated near $110 a barrel through the end of the year, an increase from its previous forecast for $100 a barrel at the end of the year.
"The impression now is that there is a significant risk premium in crude oil prices for the risk that the US/Israel will attack Iran in the coming weeks," said SEB analyst Bjarne Schieldrop.
Investors were also looking for cues from Israel's election on Tuesday, which could ‌spell the end of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's time in office, though polling ​suggested results would be close and that his Likud party could still prevail.
"The outcome ​of today's parliamentary elections in Israel could also be significant ​for further developments in the war with Iran, as Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, if re-elected, might attempt to ‌achieve regime change in Iran," Commerzbank analysts wrote.
Crude oil exports ​from Russia's Baltic and Black Sea ​ports were forecast to fall next month as domestic refiners plan to increase their output after the end of maintenance and to produce more diesel to meet the demands of a deal struck this month between Washington and Moscow, two traders said.
Russian oil ​refineries increased crude processing by 25% in the ‌second half of October compared to the beginning of the month after persistent Ukrainian drone attacks on the plants ceased, ​three people in the industry told Reuters.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Valentino Is Launching in China Its First Haute Beauté Product
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Valentino Is Launching in China Its First Haute Beauté Product
articles.content_orig:
PARIS — Valentino Beauty is broadening its push into China with the launch of a first Haute Beauté product, which will be sold exclusively in its revamped Shanghai flagship.
“It’s a tipping point for us as a brand,” said Claudia Marcocci, global president of Valentino Beauty and Mugler Beauty, and chief executive officer of Mugler Couture at L’Oréal . “Of course, we have incredible success in the western world — namely in the U.S. and Europe with fragrances. But at the moment, we are becoming a power brand in the beauty industry, which is what Valentino , as a brand, deserves to be.”
She said this never could happen without Asia, especially China, or makeup. That’s where the limited-edition Haute Beauté Go-Cushion Glow comes in.
“We’ve been playing quite successfully in makeup in China,” Marcocci continued, referring to the “prêt-à-porter” color cosmetics collection that’s been selling well there over the past three to four years, due especially to Go-Cushion Glow.
“It’s the closest you can get to a fashion accessory,” Marcocci said.
In China, Valentino ’s Go-Cushion Glow ranks sixth year-to-date, having risen four places against last year, according to the platform Beauty Research. In the second quarter of 2026, the cushion came in fifth, up six places year-over-year.
Cushions, which are portable beauty product-infused sponges held in compacts, represent a huge business. Last year, the cushion foundation market was valued at $1.45 billion, with the Asia-Pacific region generating 55 percent of that, according to Strategic Revenue Insights.
Marcocci believes Valentino’s key brand values, including femininity, strength, grace, joyfulness and craftsmanship, chime with Chinese consumers.
Another reason for Valentino’s success is that it’s playing in Asia’s major face category. Makeup is the second-largest beauty product segment there, after skin care.
An additional boost is the Go-Cushion Glow’s benefits of giving — as the name suggests — glow and light.
“It is what this brand embodies,” Marcocci said. “We always talk about the Roman light. It’s almost like a golden hour all day in Rome.”
That’s Valentino’s birthplace. She described it as a brand that “sparkles.”
“This is something we really wanted to bring and base the future strategy on, which is realigning the image of the brand,” Marcocci said, adding that includes its products, in terms of elevation.
In keeping, Valentino Beauty set out to develop a limited-edition cushion reflective of the brand’s couture heritage. The idea was “to do it in a way that is unique, exceptional, extraordinary and crafted with a design which is absolutely aligned with the [house’s] creative direction. This has never been done before in this way.”
The 10 hours of craftsmanship poured into the limited-edition cushions, of which there will be 100 numbered, unique editions on offer in the brand’s renovated Shanghai boutique starting Oct. 28, are equivalent to time spent on making a Valentino jacket.
Their celestial motif, fashioned with gold threads, beads and sequins, spangles the cushion’s lid covered with purple velvet. This was created in Valentino’s ateliers. Its price is 4,000 renminbi, or $600.
“In a world which is dominated by AI and fakes, we go back to work done by hand,” Marcocci said. “That’s the value of an haute couture brand. We have a mission of sustainability and to go back to basics.”
She said in Rome — the “eternal city” — everything is kept and treasured for the next generations. “This is what we want to do with this product,” Marcocci said.
Before makeup was industrialized in the 1960s, it was an object of desire and a piece of art passed down through families. “This is the dream we want to carry here,” Marcocci said. “It’s something that is born to last and prove the test of time.”
The cushion, which is refillable, comes in a deep purple outer lacquer box, which nods to the world of watches, and with a pouch.
Valentino entered the haute couture fragrance category, with its Anatomy of Dreams collection, two years ago.
In the U.S., Valentino’s Born in Roma Donna ranked first among women’s fragrances and Uomo second among men’s scents in August year-to-date. Worldwide, Valentino places among the top-five fragrance brands, according to Circana data.
The limited-edition cushion is also a celebration of Valentino Beauty’s renovated store in Shanghai’s Xintiandi district.
“Our motto is always ‘Color, Cool, Couture,’” Marcocci said, explaining the “color” is in the cushion product and the “cool” is the store location. She emphasized retail is not at all dead, that it just needs a point of difference from shopping online.
“With Valentino, which is warm and all about entertainment and experience, we also want to put this into the product,” Marcocci said. So the limited-edition cushion cannot be found anywhere else.
“We wanted to start with something that really is extraordinary,” Marcocci said.
The 960-square-foot store was initially opened in December 2021, under a different creative direction for Valentino.
“Today, there is a new design concept which is linked with the elevation and the entertainment of the brand,” Marcocci said.
The executive added: “We have the highest confidence and the highest belief in Alessandro and in his vision.”
She was referring to Alessandro Michele, who became the house’s artistic director in April 2024, calling him one of the “geniuses of couture of his epoch.”
Marcocci finds in China a merging of coolness and high luxury.
“There’s also an understanding of what luxury really is,” she said, explaining that it includes upping the value quotient. “This is what we are trying to convey in the new store.”
Set against an ivory backdrop, Valentino Beauty products’ colors are meant to pop there.
“At the same time, you have the full experience,” Marcocci said. “There is a sense of calm, as well.”
It is to emulate the warm feeling upon entering a Valentino store in Rome, she continued.
“This is the soul of the brand,” Marcocci said. “It’s our tone of voice. We say we are ‘couture in the street’ — in the good sense of the term. It’s a high-couture brand that speaks to people with its heart in its hand. This has been the key to our success so far.”
The new-look store is a template for other Valentino Beauty locations yet to come.
The brand has 27 of its own beauty doors, of which 25 are in China, one in Malaysia and one in Saudi Arabia. These are key to giving a 360-degree brand experience and developing personal client relationships.
“More to come,” Marcocci said. That could include more limited-edition couture beauty pieces for Valentino.
“Valentino was the first Italian brand to be invited to haute couture in Paris, so we wanted to be the first to do Haute Beauté in beauty,” she said.

articles.title_orig: Kennedy Makes Bigoted Remarks About Arabs at Michigan Campaign Event
articles.title_zh: Kennedy Makes Bigoted Remarks About Arabs at Michigan Campaign Event
articles.content_orig:
— A closer look at Kennedy's comments
October 27, 2026 • 3 min read
Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s broad assertions about Arab contributions to humanity's scientific and literary discoveries at a Republican campaign event in Grand Rapids, Michigan, have drawn criticism just days before midterm elections.
"There's 500 million Arabs in the world and yet they don't produce science," Kennedy said on the campaign trail Monday. "They don't win the Nobel Prize. They don't win the Fields Prize. They don't win the Wolf Prize. They don't produce literature."
The health secretary's comments  --  widely condemned overnight by critics as untrue and racially biased  --  were made while campaigning in a state with a large Arab American population.
An HHS representative did not immediately respond to an Associated Press request for comment.
Arab refers to an ethnic and linguistic identification, while Muslim refers to a religious identity. So while Arabs can be Muslim, Christian, Jewish, or of another faith, the vast majority of Muslims worldwide are not Arab.
Here's a closer look at Kennedy's comments.
Arabs Have Won the Nobel Prize
The Background of His Comments
Kennedy made the comments while campaigning for Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, who has accused his opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, MD , of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist organization.
El-Sayed, who has disavowed the group, has also been accused by President Donald Trump of being a Muslim Brotherhood member. Trump has also made racist comments about El-Sayed.
"Mike Rogers was talking about the Muslim Brotherhood. That's something I can talk about," Kennedy said. Kennedy argued that the world's 500 million Arabs have not contributed to science or the humanities due to the influence of the Muslim Brotherhood, after he cited Islamic civilization's contributions to literature in the 13th century.
"All that tradition has been destroyed by the Muslim Brotherhood," Kennedy said. The U.S. has labeled several Middle Eastern branches of the Muslim Brotherhood as terrorist organizations. "They've created stagnant societies that do one, two things: hatred and war and victimization," Kennedy said.
The Muslim Brotherhood was founded in Egypt in 1928 but was banned after Brotherhood-backed President Mohamed Morsi was ousted in 2013. Jordan announced a sweeping ban on the organization last year. Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Bahrain designated the organization as a terrorist group in 2014.
Protect Our Care president Brad Woodhouse said in a statement that "this wasn't the first time RFK Jr. has trafficked in racism, but it may be his ugliest episode yet." Woodhouse was referring to Kennedy's comments on the "High Level Conversations" podcast in 2024, where he implied that Black children with ADHD and on medication should be "re-parented."
Peter Hotez, MD, PhD, founding dean of the National School of Tropical Medicine at Baylor and Texas Children's Hospital, posted on social media Monday evening that his former colleague, Nobel Prize winner Zewail, would disagree with Kennedy.
"God rest his soul he didn't have to endure this, and of course RFK Jr. forgets that it was the Arab scientists of the Middle Ages who kept Aristotle, Hippocrates, Galen alive to hand it down in the Renaissance."
Kennedy is slated to serve as a special guest at the "Make Iowa Healthy Again Rally" in Des Moines on Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Will Go Parabolic on Oct. 30
articles.title_zh: Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Will Go Parabolic on Oct. 30
articles.content_orig:
As technology companies race to build data centers, demand for the memory chips that make artificial intelligence (AI) computing possible has skyrocketed. One of the leading manufacturers of memory chips for AI hyperscalers is Micron Technology ( MU +2.77% ) .
So far this year, Micron stock has soared 225% -- making it the third-highest performer in the Nasdaq-100. Nevertheless, Micron's shares have experienced considerable volatility over the last couple of months and trade about 24% below their all-time high.
I think this disconnect is about to reverse. On Oct. 28 and 29, Alphabet ( GOOGL +1.19% ) ( GOOG +0.84% ) and Amazon ( AMZN +1.61% ) are scheduled to report quarterly earnings. While investors will undoubtedly focus on their respective AI-related capital expenditures (capex), I think another topic could emerge as a major discussion point: the global memory shortage. If my prediction is accurate, Micron could begin to rally just in time for Halloween.
NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 10/27/26
For most of the AI revolution, investors primarily associated infrastructure with graphics processing units (GPUs) designed by Nvidia and application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) designed by Broadcom . However, GPUs and custom silicon cannot operate efficiently without sufficient memory. Micron manufactures dynamic random access memory (DRAM) and high bandwidth memory (HBM), both of which are critical components of the AI chip stack.
Interestingly, Amazon CEO Andy Jassy already highlighted the growing importance of memory during the company's last earnings call. Jassy explained that Amazon planned to increase its 2026 capex budget to $220 billion -- up from its previous forecast of $200 billion -- specifically because of higher memory costs.
Meanwhile, Alphabet raised its 2026 capex forecast to $195 billion to $205 billion during its second-quarter earnings call. Management attributed the increase to accelerating infrastructure investments and capacity supply constraints. Although Alphabet did not explicitly identify memory as the culprit, its comments reinforce the underlying idea that demand for AI compute is insatiable.
As both companies prepare to report earnings this week, investors should pay close attention to any additional commentary surrounding memory availability, pricing, and infrastructure spending.
Image source: Getty Images.
Amazon and Alphabet aren't the only companies confronting the memory shortage. Earlier this month, Elon Musk took to X (formerly Twitter) to discuss the bottlenecks facing AI infrastructure build-outs. Musk specifically identified RAM supply as a constraint, supporting the idea that memory availability is becoming just as important as access to advanced processors.
This distinction matters because the AI infrastructure boom is moving beyond simply procuring as many GPUs as possible. AI models need memory to support training and inference. Training involves teaching AI to recognize patterns , while inference occurs when those models are deployed to perform an actual task rather than just answer a query. Both activities require substantial memory, particularly as applications become more complex across autonomous systems, robotics, and agentic AI.
A prolonged memory shortage could create favorable conditions for Micron. When demand for a product exceeds available supply, manufacturers can command higher prices . For Micron, this is already happening and translating into accelerating revenue growth, expanding profit margins, and earnings visibility.
MU Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts
One of the biggest headwinds dragging on Micron stock right now is skepticism about the semiconductor industry's boom-and-bust cycles and whether hyperscalers can maintain the pace of their infrastructure spending. I think Amazon's and Alphabet's upcoming earnings reports will help answer that question.
If leadership explicitly emphasizes the memory shortage, rising component prices, or the increasing demand for memory-intensive AI applications, investors may begin to view Micron's growth as more durable than anticipated.
My prediction is that earnings season will become a turning point for Micron stock. If the world's largest AI developers stress the industry's memory shortage, investors should recognize that Micron's opportunity extends well beyond this year. With shares still trading meaningfully below their all-time high, positive commentary could provide a much-needed catalyst for a new rally.

articles.title_orig: Live Updates: 8-month Iran war looms over Israeli election as Egypt wades into Saudi's fight with the Houthis
articles.title_zh: Live Updates: 8-month Iran war looms over Israeli election as Egypt wades into Saudi's fight with the Houthis
articles.content_orig:
International Atomic Energy Agency chief Rafael Grossi urged Iran during a U.N. Security Council meeting on Tuesday to grant immediate access to his agency so it can verify the Islamic republic's nuclear materials.
The IAEA has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel and the United States launched strikes on nuclear sites in June 2025.
Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.
"I invite Iran to work with the IAEA without any further delay to clarify outstanding safeguards questions and to give the IAEA the information and access the agency requires, so that it can verify all relevant facilities and material, as is Iran's legal obligation," Grossi said.
The Security Council meeting followed a resolution passed by the IAEA board last month that referred Iran to the top U.N. body over its nuclear "non-compliance."
The resolution, submitted by Britain, France, Germany and the United States, marks the first time Iran has been referred to the Security Council in 20 years for failing to comply with its nuclear reporting obligations.
The move has been seen as largely symbolic as China and Russia hold power to veto any sanctions against their ally Tehran. Both countries were joined by Niger in voting against the IAEA resolution.
Nearly 100 fighters have been killed in renewed clashes between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed government forces in southwestern Yemen, military sources from both sides told the AFP news agency on Tuesday.
At least 63 Houthi fighters and 34 pro-government combatants have died, mostly near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea's strategic southern chokepoint, they said.
The clashes, which began with airstrikes late on Monday, are the fiercest since the Houthis seized swathes of territory from the Saudi-backed government in a lightning offensive last month.
The Houthis fought off "an attempted advance by Saudi enemy forces ... from the southern direction of Bab al-Mandab," military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X, describing "a large number of dead and wounded."
The Houthi military sources said Saudi Arabia carried out dozens of airstrikes, hitting Mayyun Island in the strait as well as Dhubab and Mocha further up the Red Sea coast.
Government military sources said intense fighting was under way in the Bab el-Mandeb area, claiming they had made progress on the ground.
Earlier this month, Yemen's government launched a counteroffensive with Saudi air support to try to reclaim the territory lost to the Houthis.
But the campaign has faltered, while the Houthis have ramped up deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia that shuttered its capital's airport for two weeks and disrupted daily life.
Riyadh leads a military coalition that first intervened in the conflict in 2015. The fighting has devastated Yemen and created one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Iranian counterpart, President Masoud Pezeshkian, discussed working together on oil and gas projects as the two met in person at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum Summit in Moscow on Tuesday.
The two leaders "discussed expanding political, economic, trade and energy cooperation, including joint projects in the oil and gas sectors," according to a readout from the Iranian government .
Pezeshkian also discussed working together on natural gas exports. Iran ranks third in the world in natural gas production — 280 billion cubic meters per year, according to the president — behind only the U.S. and Russia.
"Pezeshkian emphasized that global developments necessitate joint technical-engineering cooperation and strategic governance across international energy markets," the government said, presumably referring to the war with the U.S.
Russia and Iran have worked together for years. As the war in Ukraine continues, Russia continues to purchase Shahed drones for use in attacks.
The two countries have rarely coordinated on energy projects, however, as both countries produce massive amounts of crude on their own. The timing of the discussion Tuesday in Russia is especially important though because Iran has been cut off from importing or exporting crude due to the U.S. blockade on Iranian ports.
France's deputy chief of mission in Tehran was this month subjected to "intimidation by individuals claiming to belong to the Iranian security forces," a diplomatic source told the AFP news agency on Tuesday.
The incident, the second involving French diplomats in Tehran in less than four months, highlights the sharp deterioration in relations between France and Iran.
In response to the mistreatment of the diplomat in early October, Iran's ambassador to France was summoned by the French foreign ministry, the source said, without specifying the exact date of the summons.
"He was reminded in the strongest terms that we expect the Iranian authorities to take all necessary measures to guarantee the security of our personnel and premises," the source said.
French magazine Le Point , which first reported the incident, said the diplomat was forcibly stopped in the street by members of Iran's security forces, in breach of his diplomatic status. The encounter culminated in what the magazine described as a forceful interrogation.
The episode follows a July incident involving two French diplomats based in Tehran.
French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot accused the Iranian authorities at the time of having "detained them without reason for several hours," adding one of them had been "physically manhandled."
Iran said at the time the diplomats had been "briefly questioned" by security services after attending a "meeting with several individuals wanted by the authorities," and denounced French "interference … under the pretext of engaging with civil society."
The Iran-backed Houthis claimed Thursday that they struck three different airports in southwestern Saudi Arabia, and repelled an advance by Saudi-affiliated forces from the southern direction of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Houthi military spokesperson Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree said on X that the group's forces had "succeeded in targeting two military transport aircraft with two ballistic missiles: the first at Najran Airport and the second at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait," both of which are in southwestern Saudi Arabia.
"Both operations successfully achieved their objectives, by the grace of God," he added.
In a separate statement on X , Saree said Houthi forces earlier thwarted an attempted advance by what he described as Saudi enemy forces "from the southern direction of Bab al-Mandab," the gateway to the Red Sea.
"These force concentrations were targeted with a number of ballistic missiles and heavy weapons, resulting in large numbers of dead and wounded," he said.
In a third statement Tuesday, Saree claimed the Houthis had struck Abha International Airport, also in the Saudi southwest.
"The strike was accurate and led to the disruption of air traffic at the airport," he said.
An oil tanker has caught fire after being caught in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's navy said on Tuesday.
"Hours ago, a rogue oil tanker that had switched off its tracking systems and was attempting to pass through a prohibited and unsafe area east of the Strait of Hormuz struck naval mines, sustaining damage and catching fire," the navy's public relations office said.
"The Strait of Hormuz is unsafe and closed to rogue ships and vessels attempting to pass through without coordination," it added.
Iran has repeatedly said it will only allow vessels to pass through the waterway if they coordinate with authorities. The U.S. has urged shippers to use a southern route through the strait that Tehran regards as illegal.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in "perfect health," describing him as energetic, hopeful and composed following a meeting.

articles.title_orig: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
articles.title_zh: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
articles.content_orig:
Amazon laid out its AI usage guidelines for software engineers in a memo to staffers, and discouraged employees from turning to "tokenmaxxing" in their push to embrace artificial intelligence tools.
The memo , which was circulated internally in September and posted to the company's website on Tuesday, revises how the company defines the role of software development engineers and managers in the age of AI.
"We're just seeing the beginning of AI's effect on software engineering," the company wrote. "While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there's a lot that's still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice."
Under CEO Andy Jassy , Amazon has rapidly integrated AI across the company's sprawling business operations. Jassy has previously predicted that AI will "change the scope and speed" of day-to-day work, and potentially shrink its corporate workforce in the next few years through automation, though he's noted it will also create "other jobs."
As employees rush to adopt AI tools, companies have grappled with the technology's surging costs and how to reliably measure whether the technology leads to a productivity boost or other valuable returns on investment.
Companies have recently cracked down on tokenmaxxing , in which developers use AI as much as possible with little regard for output. Some companies have set limits on employees' usage of tokens, or the units of data that are processed and generated by AI models, in a bid to slow rising AI bills. Others have switched to cheaper, open-source models for certain tasks.
An Amazon spokesperson said the company hasn't instituted caps on employees' token usage. Amazon in May shut down an internal leaderboard after discovering employees were tokenmaxxing to climb the ranks.
In the memo posted Tuesday, Amazon said metrics like token usage, the rate of adoption of AI tools, and code changes or reviews remain "deeply flawed" ways of measuring teams or organizations' AI usage, adding that they can lead to higher costs and too much complexity.
It stopped short of telling staffers to ignore those metrics altogether, however. Token usage and code generation should be considered "with care and judgment" alongside other data, Amazon said.
"We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes," the company wrote.
Marc Brooker, a vice president and distinguished engineer at Amazon Web Services, told CNBC in an interview that the company has looked to metrics such as "feature velocity" to measure how AI is improving engineer productivity.
The metric looks at things like, "how many launches are we doing, how many successful changes are we making in production," he said.
"Broadly, we think about this as a return on investment," Brooker said. "If there is an important problem to solve for our customers, important problem to solve for our business, we're going to invest tools, time, tokens, human effort, etc. into those."
He added, "What we don't want to see is wasted effort where we are going and spending those tokens solving problems that don't matter and sometimes it's hard to know, so we do need to have some appetite for experimentation."
Amazon also discouraged staffers from using AI when it doesn't make sense for a given task.
"If your work does not benefit from current AI tooling, that is a finding, not a failing," Amazon said in the memo.
The company added, "An engineer who can explain where AI does not yet help their work is demonstrating the judgement we are asking for."

articles.title_zh: Norway and Finland hold rare call with Putin to discuss ending war

The leaders of Finland and Norway have held a joint call with Vladimir Putin - rare contact between the Russian president and European leaders.
Finland's President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said the aim of the call had been to "convey messages directly regarding future negotiations" towards peace. An end to the conflict in Ukraine "will not be achieved through silence," Stubb said.
Neither side suggested the needle had been moved on ending the war, which began when Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Although the Finnish leader said the conversation with Putin had been "frank and substantive," Støre added that there were "big differences in views" with Putin.
Several European leaders have recently shown willingness to engage with Russia directly, but both Stubb and Støre pointed out their initiative was taken in their capacity as neighbours of Russia, rather than on behalf of Europe as a whole.

Stubb added the call had been prepared in consultation with Ukraine and the US following a meeting between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, the Nordic leaders and US special envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo last week.
The first trilateral US-Ukraine-Russia talks since the start of the year are tentatively planned for early November in Abu Dhabi.

articles.title_orig: Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season
articles.title_zh: Amid the Anthropic IPO excitement, don't forget about earnings season
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
We are only two days into the week, and it already feels like it should be the weekend.
In the past two days, Meta ( META ) said it will raise $95 billion to support its AI build-out through stock offerings, and Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) dropped a 407-page IPO prospectus that I know you haven't read in its entirety. (Wall Street hasn't either, so don't lose sleep over it.)
Lost in that activity is that earnings season continues in full swing, with results from Coca-Cola ( KO ), Hilton ( HLT ), UPS ( UPS ), Whirlpool ( WHR ), and others today.
While investors are jacked up about AI and some stability returning to the tech trade, don't lose sight of earnings season: After all, it's earnings and earnings expectations that power stocks, not Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei (although his comments have moved markets in the past).
So here are a few quick takes on a couple of earnings reports I chewed through this morning:
I don't have any problems with this Hilton quarter, even though the stock is getting hit on a slight revenue miss. The important revenue per available room metric grew 5.8%, the company remains an aggressive buyer of its stock, and it approved the development of 30,500 rooms in the quarter.
The report fits nicely with the Delta ( DAL ) report we got last week, in that higher fuel prices don't appear to be slowing leisure or business travelers.
I think it also fits nicely with the numbers out of UPS today, with US sales up 4.5% and its full-year guidance hike.
Coca-Cola's latest guidance lift reinforces the view that the company continues to take massive market share away from rival PepsiCo ( PEP ). Coke Zero sales surged 16%.
Not a good day for the team at PepsiCo up in Purchase, N.Y.
I continue to be absolutely shocked by what's happening at Whirlpool ( WHR ). Another supersoft quarter, with an adjusted loss of $0.21 per share. Costs are up, and the business is being hurt by a near-frozen US housing market.
You need nerves of steel to buy Whirlpool shares here — the stock is down more than 63% this year. If you do, the thesis has to be that the iconic company is acquired at some point in the next 12 months.

articles.title_orig: The secret succession rankings that Anthropic shareholders will never see (unless the company is ordered)
articles.title_zh: The secret succession rankings that Anthropic shareholders will never see (unless the company is ordered)
articles.content_orig:
Anthropic has devised an unusual way for its founders to pass on their power.
In its IPO filings , Anthropic outlined how seven of its cofounders, who collectively have 50.1% of voting control, will be able to create a ranked list of who they'd like to inherit their power in the event of their death or incapacitation.
What's particularly notable is that while the names would be shared with the other LLC members and Anthropic's Nominating Committee, they are otherwise contractually confidential and generally not public.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei , Anthropic President Daniela Amodei, and the five other LLC members will review and vote on whether to approve their fellow founders' proposed successors, but the names will likely never be seen by other shareholders. (The agreement allows for the publication only in narrow circumstances, such as a court order or other legal requirement.)
Under the agreement, which was first highlighted by Forbes , each member of the Founders LLC may name up to 10 potential successors, ranked in order of preference. The other LLC members must then vote to approve the secret lists.
While succession plans are not unusual, Anthropic's approach is unusual in how it ranks potential successors. It also underscores how, thanks to the Founders LLC, Anthropic's leaders will be able to maintain control as shareholders begin to offer input post-IPO.
Facebook's 2012 IPO paperwork suggested that if Mark Zuckerberg were in control of the company at the time of his death, then control could be transferred to someone he designated. (Meta has since tweaked this plan.) In 2020, Airbnb's three cofounders agreed to transfer their voting power to their other cofounders if one of them died or became disabled, but that arrangement (which still exists) only lasts for nine months.
The succession plan does not establish CEO succession. Anthropic's board of directors would handle such a chief executive appointment.
There are also some limitations to who the Anthropic founders can name on their lists.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
Eight of their 10 potential successors are subject to eligibility requirements, including that the person named is a current or former employee of Anthropic or one of its subsidiaries, or has worked for "a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization or a national or international organization whose primary purpose is research, education, or the promotion of public benefit." In either case, the person must have worked there for at least three years.
If the person worked for Anthropic, they must have held a specific role, such as a member of the technical staff or the company's internal think tank, or another role approved by the board and a majority of the other members. If they worked outside Anthropic, they must have held a senior role at the nonprofit. These successors must also be US citizens, have permanent residency, or have valid work authorization.
The other two names, if a founder names all 10 potential successors, are not subject to the eligibility requirements, but they must also receive the required approval.
The succession plan doesn't last forever.
Under the agreement, a successor member generally would cease to be a member on the 10th anniversary of Anthropic's IPO. After that point, successor designees may be admitted only in limited circumstances during a transition period.

articles.title_orig: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
articles.title_zh: Fed meeting live updates: Federal Reserve weighs elevated inflation, midterm elections as October meeting kicks off
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
The Federal Reserve kicked off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday as elevated inflation continues to pose a problem for central bankers who nevertheless seem reluctant to hike rates this month.
Fed watchers expect the central bank to keep benchmark rates in the 3.75% to 4% range , with bond traders pricing in a less than 10% chance of a hike on Wednesday, per CME Group. A rate hike in December appears far more likely, however, according to the Fed's dot plot and fed funds futures.
Although recent inflation data came in hotter than expected , several officials' remarks suggest the Fed will hold rates this month to continue assessing additional data. The proximity of the October meeting to the US midterm elections next Tuesday is also seen as a deterrent to bold monetary policy moves.
With the Fed holding rates steady seen as all but given, the focus is on what Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will say at his post-FOMC-meeting press conference on Wednesday. Warsh has deliberately avoided telegraphing future Fed policy moves, but hot inflation could elicit more insight from him into the path forward.
The Federal Open Market Committee's two-day policy meeting has started and will conclude at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday.
The FOMC's decision on whether to cut, hold, or raise interest rates will be released at 2 p.m. tomorrow. Following that decision, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will hold a news conference at 2:30 p.m. that will be live-streamed.
This is the seventh FOMC meeting this year. The final Fed meeting of the year will take place from Dec. 8-9 and will include a Summary of Economic Projections, which will be used to gauge where policymakers see rates heading in 2027.
The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections.
Alan Blinder, a former Fed vice chair and a Princeton University economics professor, is expecting a "hawkish pause."
Although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh doesn't favor telegraphing the central bank's next move, Blinder said the moment calls for clarity.
"This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike."
The Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting kicked off this morning at 9:30 a.m. ET, as scheduled, a Fed spokesperson confirmed.
Expectations remain firm that the Fed will hold rates steady in a range of 3.75% to 4% after hiking by 25 basis points in September. Traders broadly view that the Fed will hike again in December.
But in October, there's a strong belief the Fed won't move rates. According to CME Group's FedWatch, traders see a 90% chance of no move.

articles.title_orig: Federal Reserve expected to hold interest rates steady in last decision before midterm elections
articles.title_zh: Federal Reserve expected to hold interest rates steady in last decision before midterm elections
articles.content_orig:
Navy Federal Credit Union chief economist Heather Long discusses the Federal Reserve's upcoming interest rate decisions.
The Federal Reserve is set to announce its latest interest rate decision on Wednesday with the midterm elections less than a week away.
Policymakers at the Fed say they avoid letting politics influence their monetary policy moves, and can be hesitant to hike or cut interest rates at meetings that occur ahead of the election.
Inflation has remained stubbornly high and the September consumer price index (CPI) data showed inflation rose faster than expected, with headline CPI rising 0.6% on a monthly basis and 3.7% from a year ago. The latter figure is well above the central bank's 2% inflation target.
Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, told FOX Business in an interview that while the September inflation data was hotter than expected and raised the prospects of an October rate hike, the Fed is likely to wait to "hike again in December."
CONSUMER INFLATION ROSE FASTER THAN EXPECTED IN SEPTEMBER, CPI REPORT SHOWS
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh and policymakers are expected to hold rates steady this week. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
"This hotter than expected inflation data did increase the chance of an October rate hike , but it's a very high bar to increase in October, they would do it within a week of the election. I know they like to say that they're not political, but it's a high bar for October," she explained.
"Right now, this data indicates that the Fed needs to act again, but it's not a five-alarm fire. They don't have to act immediately, they could wait until December."
"The reality is, gas prices have come down a little bit since the September highs, so we would expect the October data – you know, it won't be great, but it could be a little bit cooler than what we're seeing today. And the Fed has a reasonable case to say, we're probably still gonna hike, but let's wait a few more weeks and see just how broad-based this problem really is," Long said.
FEDERAL RESERVE HIKES INTEREST RATES FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2023 AMID STUBBORN INFLATION
The market expects the Fed to hold rates steady this week, with the CME FedWatch tool showing a 90.6% probability of rates remaining at their current target range of 3.75% to 4% – up from 84.5% a week ago and 35.8% last month.
For the Fed's meeting in mid-December, the tool shows a 75.1% probability of a 25-basis-point interest rate hike, which could mark the resumption of the rate-hiking cycle if inflation remains elevated.
WHY THE FED ISN'T READY TO DECLARE VICTORY ON INFLATION
Inflation rose faster than expected in September and remains well above the central bank's 2% target. (Robert Nickelsberg/Getty Images)
"The Federal Reserve will definitely hike interest rates again, probably in December," Long said. "The big question is how many more times do they have to hike after that? And what was scary in this latest inflation data for September is to see so many areas of hot inflation: to see used car prices, airfares, recreation costs, auto repair costs, buying a used car, medical costs."
"The story really is starting to take shape that it's probably going to take a couple more hikes in 2027, and this higher-for-longer borrowing costs and mortgage rates well above 7% is going to stick around for at least a year, maybe longer," Long said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The CME FedWatch tool shows the market is anticipating multiple rate hikes by March, with a 46.5% chance that rates will be 50 basis points higher than they are now at a range of 4.25% to 4.5%.

articles.title_orig: US consumer confidence recovers in October as gas prices eased a bit
articles.title_zh: US consumer confidence recovers in October as gas prices eased a bit
articles.content_orig:
Kitco NEWS has a diverse team of journalists reporting on the economy, stock markets, commodities, cryptocurrencies, mining and metals with accuracy and objectivity. Our goal is to help people make informed market decisions through in-depth reporting, daily market roundups, interviews with prominent industry figures, comprehensive coverage (often exclusive) of important industry events and analyses of market-affecting developments.
(Kitco News) - Gold prices are trading at session highs after the latest data showed an improving picture of the attitudes of U.S. consumers this month.
The Consumer Confidence Index rose to 91.7 in October, above economists’ consensus forecast for an 81 reading and also above the upwardly revised 84.2 print from September, the Conference Board announced on Tuesday.
The Present Situation Index—based on consumers' assessment of current business and labor market conditions—increased by 8.6 points to 120.4. The Expectations Index—based on consumers' short-term outlook for income, business, and labor market conditions—recovered by 6.9 points to 72.6, only partially reversing three consecutive monthly declines. The survey period for this month's preliminary results was October 1 - 21.
Gold prices were setting fresh session highs in the wake of the 10 am ET data release, with spot gold last trading at $4,048.48 per ounce at the time of writing for a gain of 0.78% on the daily chart.
“Consumer confidence advanced in October, driven primarily by improved perceptions of current and expected business conditions,” said Fergus McCormick, Senior Economist, Global Indicators at The Conference Board. “The recovery was in line with retail gasoline prices easing from September to October. Yet, despite the increase in October, consumer confidence remained on the long-term downward trend that's persisted over the past few years. Consumers planned less spending on services and durable goods over the next six months. This likely reflected higher price levels and persistent inflation, which eroded consumers' purchasing power.”
“Among write-in responses in October, consumers continued to express frustration with rising costs,” he added. “References to prices, the high cost of food and groceries, and oil and diesel prices rose. Comments about war and conflict eased for a second straight month but remained elevated. Mentions of jobs and employment as an area of concern also ticked up, though to a lesser extent.”
“On a six-month moving average basis, only consumers under age 35 and those with a household income of $100k or more expressed an increase in confidence,” the report noted. “By generation, confidence amongst Gen X, Baby Boomers, and the Silent Generation continued to trail significantly behind Gen Z and Millennials, widening a sharp generational divide that has emerged over the past two years. In October, confidence improved across all political affiliations—but much more so for Republicans.”
Consumers' average 12-month inflation expectations declined in October but remained elevated at 5.8%,” the Conference Board said. “Consumers still expected higher interest rates over the next 12 months. Overall, more consumers in October expected stock prices to increase rather than decrease in the next 12 months.”
Jeffrey Roach, Chief Economist at LPL Financial, noted that business conditions and discretionary spending both improved in October.
"Business conditions are the best since April when consensus believed the war with Iran would be short-lived, inflation was less sticky, and the AI-trade dominated headlines," he said. "Even more noteworthy, the top five spending plans included restaurants and movies. Several discretionary sectors are vibrant, although consumers said they will cut back on hotels and airfare."
Roach pointed out that employment opportunities also appeared more plentiful, and home buying plans improved for the third consecutive month.
"Consumers may be tightening their belts, but some experiences are still a priority," he said. "Given the other data on core capital shipments, auto sales, and broader consumer spending, Q3 economic growth will likely be above 3% as the economy plows ahead, elevating annual growth to 2.2% for the full year."
Ernest Hoffman is a Crypto and Market Reporter for Kitco News. He has over 15 years of experience as a writer, editor, broadcaster and producer for media, educational and cultural organizations. Ernest began working in market news in 2007, establishing the broadcast division of CEP News in Montreal, Canada, where he developed the fastest web-based audio news service in the world and produced economic news videos in partnership with MSN and the TMX. He has a Bachelor's degree Specialization in Journalism from Concordia University. You can reach Ernest at 1-514-670-1339.
